title: Strip a leading UTF-8 BOM when parsing a style sheet
author: X-Coder264
summary: A leading U+FEFF is tokenized as part of the first ident, so `BOM html{}` silently becomes a selector matching nothing and `BOM /*! */ html{}` or `BOM @charset` fails to parse. The PR strips it in StyleSheet::parse_with (per CSS Syntax 3.2 decode) and in the bundler before registering source content. Dart Sass compressed output with non-ASCII emits a BOM, and postcss >= 8.5.24 now preserves it, so this is hitting real builds.
evidence: Master CLI (/home/user/lightningcss/target/review/ref-574eee2/lightningcss (master 574eee2)): `\xEF\xBB\xBFhtml{color:red}` -> output still starts with the BOM glued to `html` (od shows 357 273 277 h t m l); `BOM/*! x */html{color:red}` -> parse error (CLI panics on the unwrap at main.rs:196). Issue #338 open since 2022 with several reporters; no maintainer comment. Author asks for decisions: BOM not re-emitted; napi/CLI/C source maps would be off by one column on line 1 for BOM input unless they strip too. Small, spec-backed.
